mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last two weeks (-51.7 to -31.0 to -20.6), indicating a resumption of commuting and office-linked errands that historically spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -51.7 at t-2w to -20.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise for two further consecutive weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility crossing above the -45 threshold signals relaxation of travel-limiting restrictions or reduced public caution, which mechanically permits more retail trips via public transport, raising RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -45 percent-change-from-baseline for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -53.9 at t-2w to -43.6 at t-0w, crossing -45
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays above -45 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC's mean does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects households shifting from home-centric routines back toward out-of-home activity, and this combined shift amplifies retail and recreation visits more than either series alone would predict, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises while RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -31.0 to -20.6 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.1 to 7.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues rising and RESIDENTIAL continues falling for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not exceed its last-28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During the Southern Hemisphere summer holiday period, elevated and volatile PARKS mobility (e.g. 7.4 at t-0w) indicates households substituting outdoor recreation for indoor retail and recreation visits, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated between -16.4 and 7.4 over the last four weeks while RETAIL_REC stayed flat near -16
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated (>5) for another week but RETAIL_REC's weekly mean rises rather than falls, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If a COVID-19 cluster (e.g. the Northern Beaches/Avalon outbreak) triggers renewed localized restrictions, both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES would fall sharply together, and this joint policy-driven mobility suppression would drag RETAIL_REC down within two weeks as shopping and leisure trips are curtailed by stay-at-home orders.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop more than 15 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell sharply from -32.0 to -51.7 between t-3w and t-2w, coincident with TRANSIT falling from -44.7 to -53.9
regime_hint: tightening restrictions due to local COVID cluster
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both drop sharply again but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean does not fall relative to the prior period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has been persistently elevated (8.3 to 13.1 to 11.1 to 7.1) relative to pre-pandemic baseline, indicating sustained caution and home-centric behavior that structurally caps discretionary retail and recreation trips, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained above 7 for all four observed weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 7 for the next four weeks yet RETAIL_REC's mean rises relative to the prior 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -25 percent-change, it signals a critical mass of workers returning to commuting routines, which within one week produces a corresponding uptick in lunchtime and after-work retail visits, raising RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -20.6 at t-0w, crossing above -25 for the first time in the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains above -25 for the next week but RETAIL_REC's weekly mean does not increase relative to t-0w, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising PARKS activity and falling GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests households are shifting spending from pantry-stocking toward outdoor leisure, and jointly these shifts predict a short-term dip in RETAIL_REC as discretionary shopping trips are deferred in favor of outdoor recreation during peak summer weeks.
